ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a boost-type DC-DC converter. The input power supply on the left is labeled 15 V, and a 1 mH inductor is connected in series at the input end; the node at the right end of the inductor is connected to switch Q to the lower common loop, and at the same time is connected to the output end through a diode; the output end has a 100 μF capacitor and a 10 Ω load resistor connected in parallel. The figure also labels the input resistance Rin as seen looking in from the power supply. Then reason: Given duty ratio D = 0.6, under steady state of an ideal boost converter Vout = Vin/(1-D) = 15/(1-0.6) = 37.5 V. Load current Iout = Vout/R = 37.5/10 = 3.75 A. Output power Pout = Vout^2/R = 37.5^2/10 = 140.625 W. Under ideal switch and diode, Pin = Pout, therefore input current Iin = Pin/Vin = 140.625/15 = 9.375 A. Thus the average input resistance seen by the source Rin = Vin/Iin = 15/9.375 = 1.6 Ω. To 1 decimal place it is 1.6 Ω.

method.method_draft: First identify from the image the boost converter with Vin = 15 V and load R = 10 Ω. From the text use duty cycle D = 0.6, switching frequency 25 kHz, and ideal switch/diode. Under steady-state ideal boost operation, compute Vout = Vin/(1-D) = 15/0.4 = 37.5 V. Then Iout = Vout/R = 37.5/10 = 3.75 A and Pout = Vout^2/R. With ideal components, Pin = Pout, so Iin = Pout/Vin = (37.5^2/10)/15 = 9.375 A. Finally calculate Rin = Vin/Iin = 15/9.375 = 1.6 Ω, rounded to 1 decimal place.
